'''''Valeriana rubra''''' ([[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Centranthus ruber'''''), the '''red valerian''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''spur valerian''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=8 April 2015}}</ref> '''kiss-me-quick''',<ref name=GRIN/> '''fox's brush''',<ref name=GRIN/> '''devil's beard'''<ref name="capetowninvasives.org.za">{{Cite web | url =  http://www.capetowninvasives.org.za/project/terrestrial/species/centranthus-ruber | title = Centranthus ruber - Invasive Species {{!}} Cape Town Invasives | website = www.capetowninvasives.org.za|access-date=2016-06-29|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160825211216/http://www.capetowninvasives.org.za/project/terrestrial/species/centranthus-ruber|archive-date=2016-08-25|url-status=dead}}</ref> or '''Jupiter's beard''',<ref name=GRIN/> is a popular [[garden plant]] grown for its ornamental flowers. It is not to be confused with the closely related [[Valerian (herb)|Valeriana officinalis]] (the garden valerian).  

==Description==
[[File:Centranthus ruber 1.jpg|thumb|Closeup of [[inflorescence]]]]
''Valeriana rubra'' is a multi-stemmed [[perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]] up to {{Convert|80|cm|abbr=on}} tall with red, pink or white flowers.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Harrap |first=S. |title=Harrap's Wild Flowers |publisher=Bloomsbury Wildlife |year=2025 |isbn=9781399418904 |edition=2nd}}</ref> The leaves are generally {{Convert|5-10|cm|abbr=on}} long, the stem leaves being sessile and branch leaves sometimes having a petiole up to 5 cm long. <ref>{{Cite book |last=Rose |first=F |title=Wild Flower Key |publisher=Frederick Warne |year=2006}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Poland |first=J |title=The Vegetative Key to the British Flora |last2=Clement |first2=E |publisher=John Poland |year=2009 |edition=1st}}</ref> The leaves grow in opposite pairs and are oval or [[lanceolate]] in shape. 

The inflorescences occur at the tips of the branches, in multiparous cymes with a hundred or more flowers. Each plant has either red, pink or white flowers. <ref>{{Cite book |last=Stace |first=C |title=New Flora of the British Isles |publisher=C & M Floristics |year=2019}}</ref> ''Valeriana rubra'' 'Albus' (about 10% of individuals) has white blooms. The cultivar 'coccineus' is especially long-blooming. The blooms have a strong and somewhat rank scent. 

They are pollinated by both [[bee]]s and [[butterfly|butterflies]] and the plant is noted for attracting insects.
Flowering takes place in early summer and, in cool summer areas, continues sporadically throughout the summer and into fall. Red Valerian is used as a food plant by the [[larva]]e of some [[Lepidoptera]] species including [[angle shades]]. Fruits have feathery projections similar in appearance to the pappus of [[dandelion]] seeds that allow wind dispersal, and can self-seed freely and become invasive if not properly controlled.

==Taxonomy==
''Valeriana rubra'' was the original scientific name given to the species by Linnaeus in 1753. It means 'red valerian'.  It was moved into a new genus, ''Centranthus'', in 1805, but returned again to ''Valeriana'' by 2019.  It is currently recognised by this name in the key international [https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:860141-1 Plants of the World Online database] and the [https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:860141-1 World Flora Online Plantlist]. However, the name ''Centranthus ruber'' is still a familiar gardeners' term for it, such as [https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/93739/centranthus-ruber/details at the Royal Horticultural Society]. As ''V. rubra'' is not a native of the UK and the native is ''[[Valeriana officinalis]]'', the species commonly spoken of in folk medicine, ''V. rubra'' is often spoken of as "not real Valerian" in gardening circles in the UK.{{citation needed|date=May 2026}}
==Distribution==
[[File:Centranthus ruber growing on wall (Ireland).jpg|thumb|left|Growing atop old walls in Ireland]]
''Valeriana rubra'' is native of the [[Mediterranean region]], ranging from Portugal and Spain to France, Italy, former Yugoslavia, Albania, Greece and European Turkey, and from Morocco to Algeria and Tunisia.<ref name = powo/> It has been introduced into many other parts of the world as a garden escape. It is naturalised in [[France]], [[Australia]], [[Great Britain]], [[Ireland]], [[Isle of Man]] and the [[United States]]. In the US it can be found growing wild in such western states as [[Arizona]], [[Utah]], [[California]], [[Hawaii]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], and [[Oregon]], usually in disturbed, rocky places at elevations below 200 m. It is often seen by roadsides or in urban wasteland. It can tolerate very [[alkali]]ne soil conditions.  Because of its ability to tolerate alkaline conditions, ''Valeriana rubra'' can tolerate lime in mortar, and may frequently be seen growing on old walls in Italy, southern France and south-west UK.

==Invasive species==
The species is listed as a NEMBA 1b invasive in the [[Western Cape]], [[South Africa]]. It may not be owned, imported, grown, moved, sold, given as a gift or dumped in a waterway.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.capetowninvasives.co.za/news/2014/02/nemba-invasive-alien-species-regulations-list-published-public-comment|title=NEMBA Invasive Alien Species Regulations List published for public comment|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808210359/http://www.capetowninvasives.co.za/news/2014/02/nemba-invasive-alien-species-regulations-list-published-public-comment|archive-date=2016-08-08|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="capetowninvasives.org.za"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.invasives.org.za/legislation/item/420-red-valerian-centranthus-ruber|title=Invasive Species South Africa - Protecting Biodiversity from Invasion - Red valerian {{!}} Centranthus ruber|access-date=2016-06-29|archive-date=2017-01-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170104154557/http://www.invasives.org.za/legislation/item/420-red-valerian-centranthus-ruber|url-status=dead}}</ref> It requires compulsory control as part of an invasive species control programme to remove and destroy. The plants are deemed to have such a high invasive potential that infestations can qualify to be placed under a government sponsored invasive species management programme. No permits will be issued.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sanbi.org/information-resources/infobases/invasive-alien-plant-alert|title=Invasive Alien Plant Alert {{!}} SANBI|website=www.sanbi.org|access-date=2016-06-29}}</ref>
